specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** impact-evidence-matcher
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of eight impact questions under the source of evidence that can answer it, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Impact Reporting, Usage Analytics, Reuse Tracking, Issue Tracking, Feedback Channel (all defined in this chapter above this block), and the A/B test of Chapter 16. **Evidence of Mastery:** For each question the learner commits one of five sources. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct source column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the source descriptions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Page views can answer a question about learning. (2) One source answers every question. (3) The issue list only records complaints. **Instructional Rationale:** Matching a question to its evidence source is an Understand-level action that stops a report from answering a question with the wrong data. Eight questions across five sources teach the learner what each source can and cannot say. **Content:** The five sources: Usage analytics, Reuse tracking, A/B test, Survey and feedback, Issue tracker. The eight questions (all about Watershed Basics v1.1): | # | Question | Correct source | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | How many people visited the quiz page last month? | Usage analytics | Visits are counted by analytics. | | 2 | Did another teacher adapt the simulation for their class? | Reuse tracking | Adaptation is a sign of reuse. | | 3 | Did students who used the improved version learn more? | A/B test | Only a comparison of groups can answer it. | | 4 | What do students say about the captions? | Survey and feedback | It asks for opinions in students' own words. | | 5 | How many accuracy errors were reported and fixed this year? | Issue tracker | Reports and their status are recorded there. | | 6 | Which component is opened most? | Usage analytics | Page views by component come from analytics. | | 7 | Which other course sites link to the reading? | Reuse tracking | Links with credit are a sign of reuse. | | 8 | By how much did mean learning gain differ between the versions? | A/B test | The difference of means comes from the test. | **Provenance:** The questions are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The sources follow the chapter sections "Usage Analytics", "Reuse Tracking", "Issue Tracking", and "Impact Reporting" and Chapters 16 and 17. **Rules:** Each question has exactly one correct source. Usage analytics, Reuse tracking, and A/B test hold two questions each. Survey and feedback and Issue tracker hold one each. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one question and the five sources, and may open the source descriptions. Opening them does not change the score. 2. The learner places the question under a source, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After question 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 questions in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [source]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This question is answered by [source]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can match a question to its evidence." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed question. **Starting State:** The first question in the shuffled order and the five sources. The question shown is "Which source can answer this?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter names four kinds of evidence for an impact report: reach, reuse, learning, and experience.
